10       Pending before the Court is the Report and Recommendation (“R&R”), (ECF No. 210), 
11  of United States Magistrate Judge Elayna J. Youchah, which recommends denying Defendants’ 
12  Motion for Sanctions, (ECF No. 174), and denying Plaintiff’s request for sanctions argued in its 
13  Response, (ECF No. 183).                                                  
14       A party may file specific written objections to the findings and recommendations of a 
15  United States Magistrate Judge made pursuant to Local Rule IB 1-4. 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1)(B); 
16  D. Nev. R. IB 3-2.  Upon the filing of such objections, the Court must make a de novo 
17  determination of those portions to which objections are made. D. Nev. R. IB 3-2(b).  The Court 
18  may accept, reject, or modify, in whole or in part, the findings or recommendations made by 
19  the Magistrate Judge. 28 U.S.C. § 636(b)(1); D. Nev. R. IB 3-2(b).  Where a party fails to 
20  object, however, the Court is not required to conduct “any review at all . . . of any issue that is 
21  not the subject of an objection.” Thomas v. Arn, 474 U.S. 140, 149 (1985) (citing 28 U.S.C. 
22  § 636(b)(1)).  Indeed, the Ninth Circuit has recognized that a district court is not required to 
23  review a magistrate judge’s R&R where no objections have been filed. See, e.g., United States 
24  v. Reyna–Tapia, 328 F.3d 1114, 1122 (9th Cir. 2003).                      
25       Here, no objections were filed, and the deadline to do so has passed. (See Min. Order, 
1  ECF No. 210) (setting an October 12, 2022, deadline for objections).      
2       Accordingly,                                                         
3       IT IS HEREBY ORDERED that the Report and Recommendation, (ECF No. 210), is 
4  ACCEPTED and ADOPTED in full.                                             
5       Dated this _1_3__ day of October, 2022.                              
6

                                   Gloria M. Navarro, District Judge
